manual.title: Seekonk Select Board adds Matt’s Way street-layout order to Sept. 30 agenda
manual.summary: The Seekonk Select Board is scheduled to consider an order to lay out “Matt’s Way” in the Brigham Farm III subdivision at its 6 p.m. Wednesday, Sept. 30 meeting, according to an amended agenda posted Sept. 28.
manual.body:
The Seekonk Select Board is scheduled to consider an order to lay out “Matt’s Way” in the Brigham Farm III subdivision at its 6 p.m. Wednesday, Sept. 30 meeting, according to an amended agenda posted Sept. 28.

The agenda says the proposed action would follow an as-built plan and legal description; it gives no further engineering, construction or cost details. Comparing the amended copy with the earlier version shows Matt’s Way was added as a new general-business item. The agenda also lists a public hearing on laying out Madison Court in Madison Estates, two motor-vehicle dealer license requests, a possible zoning-bylaw amendment referral and discussion of Flock cameras.

The board has not acted on these proposals; they are scheduled matters, not decisions. The meeting is set for the Select Board Meeting Room at Seekonk Town Hall, 100 Peck St. The amended notice identifies the update as posted Sept. 28 at 1:38 p.m.

Source: [Amended Select Board agenda](https://www.seekonk-ma.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_09302026-1035)

manual.title: Fall River police chief promotional assessment set for Nov. 21
manual.body:
Massachusetts Civil Service has scheduled a promotional sole assessment center for the Fall River police chief title on Nov. 21. Applications are set to open Oct. 9 and close Oct. 30, according to a state notice dated Sept. 28.

The state's assessment-center roster labels the Fall River entry “Sole AC w/In Title.” Civil Service says participating municipalities may use a sole assessment center instead of a written exam for police and fire promotions. The Fall River notice directs candidates to a separate exam poster for specific eligibility rules; the summary listing alone does not establish who may apply.

This is a scheduled examination, not an announcement that a new chief has been appointed. The notice gives no result or appointment date. Prospective candidates should consult the state notice and its linked poster for application instructions and eligibility before applying.

Sources: [Fall River assessment notice; state assessment-center roster](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/sole-assessment-center-examinations)

manual.title: Seekonk School Committee weighs $75,000 grant and strategic plan
manual.summary: Seekonk’s School Committee is scheduled to consider accepting a $75,000 Department of Elementary and Secondary Education ICP Implementation Grant and approving a strategic-plan outline at its 6 p.m. Monday, Sept. 28 meeting, according to an amended agenda posted by the district.
manual.body:
Seekonk’s School Committee is scheduled to consider accepting a $75,000 Department of Elementary and Secondary Education ICP Implementation Grant and approving a strategic-plan outline at its 6 p.m. Monday, Sept. 28 meeting, according to an amended agenda posted by the district.

The agenda also lists a first reading of the FY2028 budget calendar and second readings of four policies, including the sexual-harassment policy and policies covering the school committee-superintendent relationship and superintendent role and contract. Members are scheduled to hear updates from the superintendent, school-business administrator and student representatives.

The meeting is listed for Seekonk High School’s library/media center, 261 Arcade Ave. After public comment and other business, the committee plans to enter executive session to discuss nonunion contract negotiations and collective-bargaining strategy with the Seekonk Educators’ Association. The agenda says members will not return to open session. These are proposed agenda items, not decisions; no vote results are yet available.

A separate agenda line proposes approving a New York City senior trip dated May 18–19, 2026—dates already passed. Confirm whether the year is a typo before publishing that detail.

Source: [Amended meeting agenda](https://www.seekonk-ma.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_09282026-1034)

manual.title: Flood Watch Canceled; Taunton River Remains Above Flood Stage
manual.summary: The Taunton River near Bridgewater measured 8.42 feet at 12:45 p.m., above its 8.0-foot flood stage; the active NWS river warning says minor flooding is occurring.
manual.body:
## What's confirmed

The Taunton River near Bridgewater measured 8.42 feet at 12:45 p.m., above its 8.0-foot flood stage; the active NWS river warning says minor flooding is occurring. No new named Bristol County road closure or property impact appeared in the latest local storm reports and municipal/outlet checks through 2:24 p.m. ([NOAA/NWS gauge](https://api.water.noaa.gov/nwps/v1/gauges/BDGM3), observation valid 12:45 p.m.; [NWS river warning](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.94c26b71686a2e1b6c2b5a6b5112a9e9c1bc5fd7.001.1), issued 11:23 a.m.; [NWS local storm reports](https://api.weather.gov/products/types/LSR/locations/BOX), checked 2:24 p.m. EDT)

MEMA's 2:14 p.m. outage snapshot lists one National Grid customer without power in Rehoboth. New Bedford's earlier one-customer Eversource entry is absent from the latest file; that does not confirm restoration, and no cause is given. ([MEMA outage snapshot](http://mema.mapsonline.net/power_outage_public.csv), row updated 2:14 p.m.; checked 2:24 p.m. EDT)

## What's forecast

NWS canceled the Flood Watch at 1:52 p.m. A 1:43 p.m. update said heavy rain had ended and no additional urban or small-stream flooding was expected; the northwestern Bristol County Flood Warning expired at 1:45 p.m. The update cautioned that residual flooding could continue near small rivers and streams. ([NWS watch cancellation](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.8eb5514747ef73a77995a32fb4ae67557132a276.001.1), issued 1:52 p.m.; [NWS warning update](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.cf0e2b813b1d97e3b0a3466b9baca7f3b507e2de.001.1), issued 1:43 p.m.; EDT)

The Taunton River warning still forecasts an 8.5-foot crest this evening, then a fall below flood stage Tuesday afternoon. NWS issued a new Coastal Flood Statement at 2:08 p.m., in effect through midnight, with up to one-half foot of inundation possible in low-lying shoreline and tidal areas and some water possible on low roads or property. New Bedford's 1:54 p.m. point forecast retains showers this afternoon but projects less than 0.10 inch of additional rain. ([NWS river warning](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.94c26b71686a2e1b6c2b5a6b5112a9e9c1bc5fd7.001.1), issued 11:23 a.m.; [Coastal Flood Statement](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.2c4cd575d0e4c05d1066fdec6255170583682caa.002.1), issued 2:08 p.m.; [New Bedford forecast](https://api.weather.gov/gridpoints/BOX/81,70/forecast), updated 1:54 p.m. EDT)

manual.title: Mansfield schedules overnight hydrant flushing on 13 streets
manual.body:
Mansfield’s Water Division has scheduled overnight hydrant flushing for Tuesday, Sept. 29, across 13 streets, according to a town notice posted Sept. 28. The listed work window is midnight to 6 a.m.

The affected locations are Bicentennial Court, Hawthorne Court, Granada Circle, Evans Circle, Howe Street, Highland Avenue, Perkins Avenue, Morrow Street, Prince Street, Copeland Drive, Fox Street, Avon Street and Creeden Street. The notice identifies the schedule and streets but does not describe possible water discoloration, pressure changes or any action customers should take. The announcement appears in the town’s News Flash feed under “Hydrant Flushing Program.” The update is a practical service notice rather than a policy change; its value is the specific overnight timing for households and businesses on the listed streets. Residents seeking service-impact details should confirm directly with the town before publication.

Source: [Town of Mansfield notice](https://www.mansfieldma.com/CivicAlerts.aspx?AID=584)

manual.title: Taunton River flood watch, latest updates from the National Weather Service
manual.summary: The National Weather Service's 11:23 a.m. update says the Taunton River near Bridgewater was at 8.3 feet at 10:45 a.m., above its 8.0-foot flood stage, and reports minor flooding is occurring.
manual.body:
# Bristol County storm update — Monday, September 28, 2026, 11:29 a.m. EDT

## What's confirmed

The National Weather Service's 11:23 a.m. update says the Taunton River near Bridgewater was at 8.3 feet at 10:45 a.m., above its 8.0-foot flood stage, and reports minor flooding is occurring. The updated warning covers Bristol and Plymouth counties. [NWS Taunton River Flood Warning](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.94c26b71686a2e1b6c2b5a6b5112a9e9c1bc5fd7.001.1) (issued 11:23 a.m.; checked 11:29 a.m. EDT)

MEMA's outage file, checked at 11:29 a.m., lists one National Grid customer without power in Rehoboth (row updated 11:29 a.m.) and one Eversource customer in New Bedford (row updated 11:25 a.m.). The file does not state a cause. Westport's earlier one-customer entry is absent; that does not confirm restoration. [MEMA outage snapshot](http://mema.mapsonline.net/power_outage_public.csv) (checked 11:29 a.m. EDT)

## What's forecast

An NWS Flood Warning issued at 7:55 a.m. remains in effect for northwestern Bristol County until 1:45 p.m. Monday. It names Attleboro, North Attleborough, Taunton, and Mansfield, and says another 0.5–1 inch of rain could produce street and poor-drainage flooding. This warning is a risk statement, not confirmation of a specific local closure or property impact. [NWS northwestern Bristol Flood Warning](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.9aff2bb2567508cec2ae041aedd0c9c5315639ad.001.1) (issued 7:55 a.m.; checked 11:29 a.m. EDT)

The latest Taunton River warning forecasts a crest of 8.5 feet this evening, then a fall below flood stage Tuesday afternoon. It says that at 8.0 feet backwater flooding can affect lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro and make Woloski Park impassable to most vehicles; this is NWS impact guidance, not a separately verified new closure. [NWS Taunton River Flood Warning](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.94c26b71686a2e1b6c2b5a6b5112a9e9c1bc5fd7.001.1) (issued 11:23 a.m.; checked 11:29 a.m. EDT)

manual.title: Taunton River Flood Warning Adds a New Forecast Risk
manual.summary: At 11:53 a.m. EDT, the National Weather Service issued a Flood Warning for the Taunton River near Bridgewater, covering Bristol and Plymouth counties.
manual.body:
**Situation checked:** Sunday, September 27, 2026, 1:06 p.m. EDT

## What's confirmed

At 11:53 a.m. EDT, the National Weather Service issued a Flood Warning for the Taunton River near Bridgewater, covering Bristol and Plymouth counties. The gauge stood at 5.6 feet at 10:45 a.m., below the 8-foot flood stage. The alert itself expires at midnight, while its forecast hazard period extends through 11 p.m. Tuesday. [NWS warning](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.110b2d77e32aa712dc5d42f2a9d99cdf21eeaa76.001.1), issued 11:53 a.m.; checked 1:06 p.m. EDT.

The earlier Flood Warning for urban and small-stream flooding expired at 1 p.m. Sunday. NWS zone and Massachusetts alert feeds still showed the Coastal Flood Advisory and Flood Watch with no change at 1:06 p.m. [Expired NWS warning](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.aecf0539300e114c666f8e4528e286f98196e39b.001.1), issued 9:56 a.m.; [current NWS alerts](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/active?area=MA), checked 1:06 p.m. EDT.

MEMA's latest town-level rows, updated at 12:59 p.m., listed 17 customers without power: 9 in Easton and 8 in Rehoboth. The 10:09 a.m. snapshot listed 26 across Easton, Rehoboth, Fall River and New Bedford; Fall River and New Bedford are absent from the newer rows, which does not independently establish zero outages. Mass.gov says the MEMA map excludes municipally owned utilities and does not show interruptions by road. [MEMA outage data](http://mema.mapsonline.net/power_outage_public.csv), rows updated 12:59 p.m., checked 1:06 p.m.; [Mass.gov outage-map limitations](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/power-outages), checked 1:06 p.m. EDT.

No new Bristol County road closure, evacuation or confirmed flooding report was identified in the municipal, Mass511 and local-news checks completed by 1:03 p.m. EDT; previously reported preparation and localized flooding remain as documented in the earlier update. [Mass511 events](https://www.mass511.com/list/events), checked 1:03 p.m. EDT.

## What's forecast

NWS expects the river to rise above flood stage late Sunday, crest near 9.4 feet early Monday afternoon, and fall below flood stage Tuesday afternoon. At 9 feet, the warning describes possible backwater flooding at lower Purchade Brook and Woloski Park in Middleboro; those are forecast impacts, not a report of flooding or a closure now. [NWS warning](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.110b2d77e32aa712dc5d42f2a9d99cdf21eeaa76.001.1), issued 11:53 a.m.; checked 1:06 p.m. EDT.

manual.title: NWS Flood Warning Covers North-Central Bristol County as Rain Continues
manual.summary: At 9:56 a.m. EDT, the National Weather Service Boston/Norton issued a Flood Warning through 1 p.m. for North Central Bristol County and parts of Norfolk, Plymouth and Suffolk counties.
manual.body:
**Situation checked:** Sunday, September 27, 2026, 10:09 a.m. EDT

## What's confirmed

At 9:56 a.m. EDT, the National Weather Service Boston/Norton issued a Flood Warning through 1 p.m. for North Central Bristol County and parts of Norfolk, Plymouth and Suffolk counties. The alert says radar showed heavy rain, 2–3 inches had fallen in the warned area, and urban or small-stream flooding was ongoing or expected shortly. The alert does not identify a specific Bristol County town or street. [NWS active alert](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.aecf0539300e114c666f8e4528e286f98196e39b.001.1), issued 9:56 a.m.; checked 10:09 a.m.

MEMA's town-level outage snapshot listed 26 customers without power across four Bristol County communities: Easton had 21, Rehoboth 2, Fall River 2 and New Bedford 1. The Fall River and Easton rows were last updated at 9:59 a.m.; New Bedford's Eversource Eastern MA row was updated at 9:55 a.m. [MEMA outage data](http://mema.mapsonline.net/power_outage_public.csv), checked 10:09 a.m. EDT.

On September 26, *Dartmouth Week* reported some residents describing deep street puddles and a few power losses that had been restored by Saturday; its story also showed flooding at Apponegansett Beach. WHDH's September 26 Fall River report documented cones on flood-prone streets and preparedness, not confirmed flooding or a named closure. [Dartmouth Week](https://dartmouth.theweektoday.com/node/159632), published Sep 26; [WHDH](https://whdh.com/news/fall-river-prepared-for-possibility-of-localized-flooding-from-fall-noreaster/), published Sep 26.

DCR said the Thomas E. Pettey Causeway to Gooseberry Island in Westport would close at 8 p.m. September 25 until further notice; no reopening notice was found in this pass. The Division of Marine Fisheries' September 25 notice closed statewide shellfish growing areas effective 30 minutes before sunrise September 26, until DMF changes them to open status. [DCR advisory](https://www.mass.gov/advisory/dcr-recreational-advisory-thomas-e-pettey-causeway), issued Sep 25; [DMF closure notice](https://www.mass.gov/doc/92526-statewide-shellfish-closure-due-to-coastal-storm/download), issued Sep 25.

## What's forecast

The NWS Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect for Southern Bristol County through 8 p.m. Sunday, with up to one-half foot of inundation possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. This is a forecast risk, not confirmation of flooding at a particular location. [New Bedford NWS forecast](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?FcstType=text&bw=1&lat=41.6498&lon=-70.9264), last updated 7:24 a.m.; alert feed checked 10:09 a.m. EDT.

The Flood Watch remains in effect through 2 a.m. Tuesday, September 29. NWS expects 2–4 inches of storm-total rain, with localized 5–7-inch amounts possible; the New Bedford point forecast calls for showers and possible thunderstorms Sunday, with showers likely Monday. [NWS Flood Watch](https://api.weather.gov/alerts/urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.502052aea489cc6714da12d1b9b26725753af794.001.1), issued 2:48 a.m.; [New Bedford point forecast](https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?FcstType=text&bw=1&lat=41.6498&lon=-70.9264), updated 7:24 a.m.; checked 10:09 a.m. EDT.
